Formulation
A young adult female presents with a new-onset, left-sided throbbing headache with photophobia and variable intensity consistent with probable migraine. No prior headache history noted. Contributory factors include recent work-related stress. Family history of migraines and hypertension is noted. No systemic or neurological symptoms suggestive of serious underlying pathology. Allergic reaction to aspirin limits analgesic options. Protective factors include social support from housemates and stable contraceptive use.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Acute migraine-like headache
- Patient Goal(s): Achieve effective headache relief and return to normal activities; recognize headache triggers; monitor for symptom changes
- Clinical Goal(s): Manage headache symptomatically, assess for headache pattern, and exclude serious causes
- Actions (Patient): Take prescribed analgesics (Paracetamol and Ibuprofen as advised), maintain hydration, track headache frequency and characteristics, monitor temperature with thermometer at home, seek urgent care if headache worsens or associated symptoms develop (fever, rash, neurological signs)
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Prescribe appropriate analgesics excluding aspirin; advise on hydration and self-monitoring; recommend blood pressure check; provide education on headache triggers and symptoms warranting urgent review; arrange follow-up if headaches persist or worsen; consider referral for further assessment if headaches become recurrent or cyclical

Secondary Problem: Work-related stress
- Patient Goal(s): Identify and manage work stress to reduce its impact on well-being
- Clinical Goal(s): Support patient to acknowledge stress and explore coping strategies
- Actions (Patient): Monitor stress levels and note any correlation with headache or mood changes
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide brief supportive advice on stress management; consider further psychological support if indicated during follow-up

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Headache characteristics, probable migraine, analgesic use avoiding aspirin, hydration, importance of monitoring temperature and symptoms, signs necessitating urgent medical review (worsening headache, fever, rash)
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increasing headache severity, new neurological symptoms, high temperature, development of rash
- Coping Strategies: Avoidance of bright light, rest in darkened room, hydration, avoidance of known migraine triggers if identified
